title: Power Automate process mining: tabs and customisable layouts in the process intelligence experience
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the Microsoft documentation read for this check. Its licensing qualifications, record-reassignment guidance and narrowly stated documentation gaps are supported; no corrections are required.

claims.claim: The process intelligence experience is the next-generation process-analysis interface in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The experience enhances the previous single fixed process overview with configurable tabs.
claims.quote: The new experience enhances the previous process overview. ... Flexibility: Create multiple tabs with different card configurations instead of a single fixed view.

claims.claim: Each process view can have an independent set of analytical tabs.
claims.quote: You can have an independent set of analytical tabs per view.

claims.claim: Each tab holds its own collection of cards and visualizations.
claims.quote: Each tab maintains its own collection of cards, visualizations, and layout configuration

claims.claim: Users can arrange cards themselves.
claims.quote: Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards

claims.claim: Users can resize cards themselves.
claims.quote: Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards

claims.claim: Users can configure cards themselves.
claims.quote: Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards

claims.claim: The (+) button creates a new tab.
claims.quote: At the end of the tab bar, select (+). The Add tab dialog opens.

claims.claim: The Edit tabs menu also offers tab creation.
claims.quote: Add tab button: + Add tab option at the bottom.

claims.claim: A tab can be renamed.
claims.quote: Rename tab: Change the tab's name.

claims.claim: A tab can be duplicated.
claims.quote: Duplicate tab: Create a copy of the tab with all its cards and layout.

claims.claim: A tab can be deleted.
claims.quote: Delete tab: Remove the tab from the dashboard.

claims.claim: Tabs can be moved to change their order.
claims.quote: Move up: Shift the tab one position to the left in the tab bar. ... Move down: Shift the tab one position to the right in the tab bar.

claims.where: What's changing; Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Make public is a per-tab option that shares the tab with other users.
claims.quote: Each tab in the list has an ellipsis (...) that opens a context menu ... Make public: Share the tab with other users (indicated by person icon with lock).

claims.claim: Edit layout opens layout-editing mode.
claims.quote: To begin to customize your layout, select Edit layout in the top-right corner of the interface. This action enables edit mode

claims.claim: Cards are added from the Add card panel in edit mode.
claims.quote: In edit layout mode, the Add card panel appears on the right side of the interface. ... In the Add card panel, select a card type tile.

claims.claim: KPI is an available card type.
claims.quote: KPI: Display key performance indicators with large numeric values

claims.claim: Donut chart is an available card type.
claims.quote: Donut chart: Show proportional data in a circular, segmented format.

claims.claim: Process map is an available card type.
claims.quote: Process map: Visualize the process flow with activities and connections.

claims.claim: Vertical bar chart is an available card type.
claims.quote: Vertical bar chart: Compare values across categories using vertical bars.

claims.claim: Horizontal bar chart is an available card type.
claims.quote: Horizontal bar chart: Compare values using horizontal bars.

claims.claim: Line chart is an available card type.
claims.quote: Line chart: Display trends and changes over time.

claims.claim: Statistical grid is an available card type.
claims.quote: Statistical grid: Present detailed data in a tabular format.

claims.claim: Variant DNA is an available card type.
claims.quote: Variant DNA: Analyze process variant patterns and characteristics

claims.claim: Cards move on a grid-based layout.
claims.quote: The layout system uses a grid-based arrangement, which allows cards to snap to alignment positions as you move them.

claims.claim: Filters on a tab apply to all its cards.
claims.quote: Filters apply to all cards and visualizations on the current tab.

claims.claim: Persistent filters are saved with the tab layout.
claims.quote: Add persistent filters: Button to create filters that apply across all cards. They're saved with the tab layout

claims.claim: Persistent filters cannot be removed while viewing the tab.
claims.quote: They're saved with the tab layout and can't be removed when viewing the tab.

claims.claim: Process views can be defined in the Process Mining desktop application.
claims.quote: Process views can be defined in the Process Mining desktop application.

claims.claim: The tab-management page labels its layout-page link as preview.
claims.quote: Customize layouts in process intelligence studio (preview)

claims.claim: Microsoft does not identify which specific cards or functions remain in preview.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "public" access preview cards; read tab management, overview, dynamic layout and card overview. The preview link names no individual preview cards or functions.

claims.claim: The overview says specific tabs or whole dashboard configurations can be shared with team members.
claims.quote: Collaboration: Share specific tabs or entire dashboard configurations with team members.

claims.claim: The public-tab audience and its interaction with underlying process access are not specified beyond sharing with other users.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "public" access preview cards; "process intelligence" "sharing" "Dataverse" "API". Read tab management, overview, process sharing and security; none defines public-tab access inheritance.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No admin UI switch or API for turning this experience on or off or restricting tab sharing is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" admin disable enable switch tab sharing settings Power Platform API Dataverse; "process intelligence" "sharing" "Dataverse" "API". Read overview, tabs, layouts and returned settings/sharing excerpts; no such control.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Security & identity; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Process mining access follows environment security and Dataverse security roles and privileges.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.claim: The Environment Maker role can create, share and contribute to processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.claim: The Process Mining User role can only view created process reports.
claims.quote: The Process Mining User security role can only view created process reports.

claims.claim: Process Mining Application is an internal role that must not be assigned to users.
claims.quote: The Process Mining Application is an internal security role that process mining uses. ... Don't assign this security role to users.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to modify Process Mining User privileges.
claims.quote: Don't modify the set of privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application security roles.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to modify Process Mining Application privileges.
claims.quote: Don't modify the set of privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application security roles.

claims.claim: Conditional Access restricting Power Automate must include both Power Apps and Power Automate in Cloud apps; Power Automate alone is insufficient.
claims.quote: the following apps must be included in Cloud apps policy application: ... Power Apps ... Power Automate ... Currently, having conditional access to only Power Automate isn't enough.

claims.claim: The feature pages describe analysis and visualization, not autonomous actions on tenant data.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "actions". Read overview, tab management and dynamic layout; described operations configure dashboards, visualizations and filters, not autonomous tenant-data actions.

claims.claim: Disabling a process owner's account does not automatically make a co-owner the owner.
claims.quote: When a process owner's account is disabled, the co-owner of the process doesn't automatically become a new process owner.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.

claims.claim: Power Automate Premium is a per-user licence.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license is a per-user license

claims.claim: Each Premium licence adds 50 MB of process mining capacity.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity

claims.claim: Premium process mining capacity accumulates in a tenant-wide pool.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool

claims.claim: Premium licences contribute up to 100 GB, after which an add-on is needed to process more data.
claims.quote: up to a total of 100 GB. When you reach 100 GB, you need to purchase the Power Automate Process Mining add-on to process more data.

claims.claim: The Process Mining add-on is tenant-wide.
claims.quote: The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license.

claims.claim: The Process Mining add-on adds 100 GB to the process mining capacity pool.
claims.quote: An extra 100 GB of process mining capacity to the capacity pool, which users with the Power Automate Premium license can use.

claims.claim: The process mining overview describes a 90-day Power Automate trial.
claims.quote: For a limited time of 90 days, the Power Automate trial license offers:

claims.claim: The overview gives trial process mining capacity as 100 MB per process.
claims.quote: The trial offers limited process mining capacity of 100 MB per process.

claims.claim: The licensing FAQ instead describes a free 30-day Process Mining trial.
claims.quote: Yes, Process Mining offers a free 30-day trial giving access to many of the key features of Process Mining.

claims.claim: The FAQ says the Process Mining trial is included in the Power Automate trial.
claims.quote: The free Process Mining trial is included in the Power Automate trial.

claims.claim: The overview names Power BI Premium and linking to one's own Power BI workspace for report customization.
claims.quote: To customize your report, you need to link the process to your own Power BI workspace, and a Power BI Premium license.

claims.claim: The FAQ instead identifies Power BI Pro, Power BI per user or Power BI premium capacity as possible licences for further customization and analysis.
claims.quote: In order to customize and analyze your process mining results further, you might want to acquire more Power BI Pro*, Power BI per user, or Power BI premium capacity licenses if you haven't already done so.

claims.claim: Power BI licences are not included in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: Power BI licenses aren't included in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No meter or price specific to the process intelligence experience is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" licensing price meter capacity storage tabs cards; "process intelligence experience" "license". Read feature pages, process mining licensing overview and licensing FAQ; product pricing exists, but no experience-specific meter or price.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature's tab, layout and overview pages name no licence, and no separate licence for this experience is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "license"; "process intelligence experience" licensing price meter capacity storage tabs cards. Read tab management, dynamic layout, experience overview, product licensing overview and FAQ; found product licences only.

claims.claim: Stored process data mostly uses Dataverse file capacity.
claims.quote: The process data we store uses mostly file capacity.

claims.claim: Importing process data can exhaust Dataverse storage capacity.
claims.quote: Depending on the size of the process data you import, you might run out of Dataverse storage capacity.

claims.claim: The documentation does not describe extra cards and tabs as consuming additional capacity.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "capacity"; "process intelligence experience" licensing price meter capacity storage tabs cards. Read feature pages, process mining overview and licensing FAQ; no card/tab-specific capacity statement.

claims.claim: Process mining prerequisites include the licences or trials required for the capabilities used.
claims.quote: The required licenses or trials depending on the capabilities you want access to.

claims.claim: Process mining requires a Power Platform environment with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Power Platform environment with a Microsoft Dataverse database.

claims.claim: Administrators and system customizers can access all processes created in the environment.
claims.quote: Administrators and system customizers can access all processes created in the environment.

claims.claim: A default process view is provided automatically after process creation.
claims.quote: Default view is provided automatically after the creation of the process.

claims.claim: Changes made in Edit layout can be saved to the tab.
claims.quote: Save changes made in edit layout mode by selecting Save when exiting edit mode.

claims.claim: Some Dataverse privileges are set by default so built-in roles can use process mining without further administrator action.
claims.quote: Some privileges are set by default in Dataverse. This allows built-in security roles to use the process mining capability without further actions from system administrators.

claims.claim: The sharing page documents Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Reassign records for a departing owner's records.
claims.quote: Select the environment where the process is located. ... On the command bar, select Settings. ... Under Users + permissions, select Users. ... Select the leaving user. ... On the command bar, select Reassign records.

claims.claim: The receiving user needs appropriate privileges for the transferred entities; Environment Maker is sufficient for a process mining process.
claims.quote: The target user should have the appropriate privileges on the different entities associated with the transferred records. For process mining process, giving the Environment Maker role is sufficient.

claims.claim: The cited sharing page does not state the administrator role required for its reassignment path.
claims.quote: Searched: "process mining" "Reassign records" administrator role. Read Share process mining processes, including reassignment steps and limitations; it says administrator, but names no required administrator security role for that path.

claims.claim: Dataverse documents ReassignObjectsSystemUser for reassigning all records owned by a specified user, a general operation rather than a process-only transfer.
claims.quote: Reassigns all records that are owned by a specified user to another security principal (user, team, or organization).

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no new data source introduced by this analysis interface.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "data source". Read experience overview, tabs and layouts plus returned card and process-ingestion excerpts; none identifies a new data source introduced by the experience.
